items.title: Adam Smith
items.body: Adam Smith’s theory of economics and metaphors of an invisible hand has been used to justify laissez faire economic policies.
items.lesson: People act out of self-interest.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Classical Economics, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Every man is, no doubt, by nature, first and principally recommended to his own care; and as he is fitter to take care of himself than of any other person, it is fit and right that it should be so.”

items.title: Albert Camus
items.body: Albert Camus worked across Ethics, Humanity, Justice, Politics.
items.lesson: In a universe without meaning and purpose, it is absurd that we expect our lives to have meaning.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Existentialism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “There is but one truly serious philosophical problem, and that is suicide. Judging whether life is or is not worth living amounts to answering the fundamental question of philosophy.”

items.title: Anaximander
items.body: Anaximander worked across Metaphysics, Astronomy, Geometry, Geography.
items.lesson: The earth is hanging in space, equidistant to all other things, and is a cylindrical solid.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Pre-Socratic, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Into that from which things take their rise they pass away once more, as is ordained; for they make reparation and satisfaction to one another for the injustice according to the appointed time.”

items.title: Angela Davis
items.body: Angela Davis worked across Prison–industrial Complex, Socialism, Racism.
items.lesson: The US prison system more closely resembles a new form of slavery than a criminal justice system.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Critical Theory, then read the wiki.
items.example: ““Woman” was the test, but not every woman seemed to qualify. Black women, of course, were virtually invisible within the protracted campaign for woman suffrage. As for white working-class women, the…”

items.title: Anna Julia Cooper
items.body: Anna Julia Cooper worked across Black Feminism.
items.lesson: The greatness of a nation should not be judged by its material wealth but by the degree to which it adheres eternal truths.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Sociology, then read the wiki.
items.example: “One muffled strain in the Silent South, a jarring chord and a vague and uncomprehended cadenza has been and still is the Negro. And of that muffled chord, the one mute and voiceless note has been…”

items.title: Anne Conway
items.body: Anne Conway worked across Theology, Ontology.
items.lesson: There are three “species:” God, the source of all being, Christ, the “middle nature,” and “creature.”
items.takeaway: Snapshot Monadism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “I say, life and figure are distinct attributes of one substance, and as one and the same body may be transmuted into all kinds of figures; and as the perfecter figure comprehends that which is more…”

items.title: Aristotle
items.body: Aristotle worked across Biology, Zoology, Physics, Metaphysics, Logic, Ethics, Rhetoric, Music, Poetry, Theatre, Politics, Government.
items.lesson: We can only philosophize about the world we live in.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Aristotelianism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “All men by nature desire to know. An indication of this is the delight we take in our senses; for even apart from their usefulness they are loved for themselves; and above all others the sense of…”

items.title: Arthur Schopenhauer
items.body: Arthur Schopenhauer worked across Metaphysics, Aesthetics, Ethics, Phenomenology, Morality, Psychology.
items.lesson: Time and space are what allow for differentiation.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Post-Kantian, then read the wiki.
items.example: “All truth passes through three stages. First, it is ridiculed. Second, it is violently opposed. Third, it is accepted as being self-evident.”

items.title: Auguste Comte
items.body: Auguste Comte worked across Encyclopedic Law, Altruism, Positivism.
items.lesson: Human progress can be divided into three key stages: theological, metaphysical, and positivist.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Positivism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The object of all true Philosophy is to frame a system which shall comprehend human life under every aspect, social as well as individual. It embraces, therefore, the three kinds of phenomena of…”

items.title: Augustine of Hippo
items.body: Augustine of Hippo worked across Christianity, Metaphysics.
items.lesson: Time is experienced as a transpiring for living things but not for God.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Neo-Platonism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “An unjust law is no law at all.”

items.title: Ayn Rand
items.body: Many on the modern right have taken inspiration from Ayn Rand, particularly her advocation for rational self-interest and radical individualism.
items.lesson: Humans are heroic and one's own happiness is the moral purpose of life.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Objectivism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Remember also that the smallest minority on earth is the individual. Those who deny individual rights, cannot claim to be defenders of minorities.”

items.title: Baruch Spinoza
items.body: Baruch Spinoza worked across Ethics, Epistemology, Metaphysics.
items.lesson: Methods of mathematics should be applied to reality to create true understanding.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Rationalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “A free man thinks of death least of all things; and his wisdom is a meditation not of death but of life.”

items.title: bell hooks
items.body: bell hooks worked across Politics, Sociology, Feminism.
items.lesson: If the goal of feminism is to make women equal to men, it is not possible, because not all men are equal.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Intersectionality, then read the wiki.
items.example: “There will be no mass-based feminist movement as long as feminist ideas are understood only by a well-educated few.”

items.title: Bertrand Russell
items.body: Bertrand Russell worked across Epistemology, Ethics, Logic, Mathematics, Metaphysics, History of Philosophy, Philosophy of Language, Philosophy of Logic, Philosophy of Mathematics, Philosophy of Mind, Philosophy of Perception, Philosophy of Religion, Philosophy of Science.
items.lesson: Mathematics comes out of logic.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic Philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Men fear thought as they fear nothing else on earth – more than ruin, more even than death.”

items.title: Betty Friedan
items.body: Betty Friedan worked across Politics, Psychology, Feminism, Media.
items.lesson: Women are as capable as men for any kind of work or any career.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Feminism, then read the wiki.
items.example: ““Is this all?””

items.title: Carl Jung
items.body: Carl Jung worked across Analytical Psychology, Psychological Types, Collective Unconscious.
items.lesson: Many of the decisions made by humans are not made by conscious decision making but rather by unconscious factors passed down through generations.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Psychoanalysis, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The great problems of life — sexuality, of course, among others — are always related to the primordial images of the collective unconscious. These images are really balancing or compensating factors…”

items.title: Cicero
items.body: Cicero worked across Politics, Law, Rhetoric.
items.lesson: Republicanism is the best form of government.
items.takeaway: Snapshot the thinker, then read the wiki.
items.example: “For there is but one essential justice which cements society, and one law which establishes this justice. This law is right reason, which is the true rule of all commandments and prohibitions.”

items.title: Damaris Cudworth Masham
items.body: Damaris Cudworth Masham worked across Metaphysics, Logic, Theodicy, Universal Language.
items.lesson: It would benefit all humankind if women were allowed to receive higher education as women, primarily, educate young children.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Christian Theology, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The improvements of Reason, however requisite to Ladies for their Accomplishment, as rational Creatures; and however needful to them for the well Educating of their Children, and to their being…”

items.title: Dante Alighieri
items.body: Dante Alighieri worked across Theology, Politics, Ethics.
items.lesson: Every “substantial form” proceeds from God, and participates in His divine nature according to its nobility.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Christian Philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Now the kind of philosophy under which we proceed in the whole and in the part is moral philosophy or ethics; because the whole was undertaken not for speculation but for practice.”

items.title: David Hume
items.body: David Hume worked across Epistemology, Metaphysics, Ethics, Aesthetics, Philosophy of Mind, Political Philosophy, Philosophy of Religion, Classical economics.
items.lesson: Experience is the sole way that knowledge of anything outside ourselves arises.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Empiricism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “In our reasonings concerning matter of fact, there are all imaginable degrees of assurance, from the highest certainty to the lowest species of moral evidence. A wise man, therefore, proportions his…”

items.title: Denis Diderot
items.body: Denis Diderot worked across Science, Art.
items.lesson: Scepticism is the first step on the path toward truth
items.takeaway: Snapshot French Materialism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “To attempt the destruction of our passions is the height of folly. What a noble aim is that of the zealot who tortures himself like a madman in order to desire nothing, love nothing, feel nothing,…”

items.title: Diogenes
items.body: Diogenes worked across Asceticism, Cynicism.
items.lesson: The difference between true and false values is what matters.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Cynicism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The noblest people are those despising wealth, learning, pleasure and life; esteeming above them poverty, ignorance, hardship and death.”

items.title: Edmund Burke
items.body: Edmund Burke worked across Social Philosophy, Political Philosophy.
items.lesson: No mind can possibly understand society for it is too big and complex.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Conservatism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The writers against religion, whilst they oppose every system, are wisely careful never to set up any of their own.”

items.title: Edmund Husserl
items.body: Edmund Husserl worked across Epistemology, Ontology.
items.lesson: Our consciousness for sure exists, we should begin there and build a larger picture of reality.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Phenomenology, then read the wiki.
items.example: “First, anyone who seriously intends to become a philosopher must "once in his life" withdraw into himself and attempt, within himself, to overthrow and build anew all the sciences that, up to then,…”

items.title: Thomas Aquinas
items.body: Thomas Aquinas worked across Metaphysics, Logic, Theology, Mind, Epistemology, Ethics, Politics.
items.lesson: Faith is independent from reason; believe provides answers to questions that are undecidable by reason alone.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Thomism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Reason in man is rather like God in the world.”

items.title: Thomas Hobbes
items.body: Thomas Hobbes famous for his claim that the state of nature is “a war of all against all” that required a Leviathan to establish order. Hobbes’s worldview has been referenced to justify a muscular foreign policy.
items.lesson: Matter in motion comprises the universe and nothing else; the universe is a large mechanism.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Social Contract, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The condition of man…is a condition of war of everyone against everyone.”

items.title: Thomas Kuhn
items.body: Thomas Kuhn worked across Philosophy of Science, Historiographical externalism.
items.lesson: To understand how science unfolds we must look at its history, not just logic.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic, then read the wiki.
items.example: “"Normal science" means research firmly based upon one or more past scientific achievements, achievements that some particular scientific community acknowledges for a time as supplying the foundation…”

items.title: Thomas Nagel
items.body: Thomas Nagel worked across Politics, Ethics, Philosophy of Mind, Epistemology.
items.lesson: We cannot completely assume a ”view from nowhere,” that is completely abandon our subjectivity.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Analytic philosophy, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Eventually, I believe, current attempts to understand the mind by analogy with man-made computers that can perform superbly some of the same external tasks as conscious beings will be recognized as…”

items.title: Voltaire
items.body: Voltaire worked across Politics, Religion, Historiography, Skepticism.
items.lesson: Every fact and theory in history has been revised at some point.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Deism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Divorce is probably of nearly the same age as marriage. I believe, however, that marriage is some weeks the more ancient.”

items.title: W. E. B. Du Bois
items.body: W. E. B. Du Bois worked across Politics, Sociology, History.
items.lesson: We aspire to a broader fuller life.
items.takeaway: Snapshot the thinker, then read the wiki.
items.example: “To be a poor man is hard, but to be a poor race in a land of dollars is the very bottom of hardships.”

items.title: Walter Benjamin
items.body: Walter Benjamin worked across Aesthetics, Philosophy of Language.
items.lesson: We construct our lives more out of facts than out of convictions.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Western Marxism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “A religion may be discerned in capitalism—that is to say, capitalism serves essentially to allay the same anxieties, torments, and disturbances to which the so-called religions offered answers.”

items.title: Wilhelm von Humboldt
items.body: Wilhelm von Humboldt worked across Philosophy of Language.
items.lesson: The power of the state to restrict individual liberties should be limited to preventing harm done to others.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Classical Liberalism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The inquiry into the proper aims and limits of State agency must be of the highest importance—nay, that it is perhaps more vitally momentous than any other political question.”

items.title: William James
items.body: William James worked across Pragmatism, Psychology, Philosophy of Religion, Epistemology, Meaning.
items.lesson: Something can be said to be true if it does all of its required jobs (conforms to known facts, yields insights/predictions, etc.) is true.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Pragmatism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “All our scientific and philosophic ideals are altars to unknown gods.”

items.title: William of Ockham
items.body: William of Ockham worked across Metaphysics, Epistemology, Theology, Logic, Ontology, Politics.
items.lesson: Logic differs from the natural order of things as necessity exists in the former but not the later.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Scholasticism, then read the wiki.
items.example: “It is pointless to do with more what can be done with fewer.”

items.title: Xenophanes
items.body: Xenophanes worked across Theology, Metaphysics, Epistemology.
items.lesson: While we may get closer to truth, it is a creation of humankind and thus conjecture.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Pre-Socratic, then read the wiki.
items.example: “Mortals deem that the gods are begotten as they are, and have clothes like theirs, and voice and form.”

items.title: Zeno
items.body: Zeno worked across Metaphysics, Ontology.
items.lesson: Even a logical argument can render a false conclusion.
items.takeaway: Snapshot Eleatic school, then read the wiki.
items.example: “The truth is, that these writings of mine were meant to protect the arguments of Parmenides against those who make fun of him and seek to show the many ridiculous and contradictory results which…”
